style: Output a single polished 16:9 game screenshot / key-art frame. No UI text, no logos, no watermarks, no HUD numbers. Same scene content as described, only the ART DIRECTION differs. The image must look like something a small team could plausibly ship as a real-time game, with believable rendering cost (no impossible detail density).

jobs.name: A_lowpoly
jobs.track: art direction A: faceted low-poly flat-shaded
jobs.prompt: Game key art for a sandbox game called 'Third Life'. SCENE (identical for every art direction): third-person camera slightly behind and above a small player avatar standing on a grassy ridge at golden hour, holding a glowing holographic tablet (the 'designer'). Below in the valley: (1) an ICE-HOCKEY ARENA UNDER CONSTRUCTION - half-built roof ribs, scaffolding, cranes, and a dozen small glowing builder-robot agents working, with unfinished sections shown as translucent holographic blueprint wireframe; (2) a winding RACE CIRCUIT with two cars, one spitting a nitro flame, a concrete barrier section crumbling into chunks; (3) a modest player-built wooden house with a half-finished extension. ART DIRECTION A: faceted LOW-POLY, flat shaded polygons with no textures, soft gradient sky, simple ambient occlusion, limited harmonious palette, very readable silhouettes (think Monument Valley meets modern low-poly strategy art).
